[Drag and Drop with dynamically changing sizes | by Michael Chen | Medium](https://medium.com/@michaelchen101/draft-drag-and-drop-with-dynamically-changing-sizes-cedb3f479038)\n\n# dnd-kit vs react-beautiful-dnd for Grid Drag-Drop Portfolios\n\n## Overview\n\n**dnd-kit** is a modern, lightweight drag-and-drop toolkit that's become the preferred alternative to react-beautiful-dnd for building drag-drop interfaces including grid portfolios.[1][2]\n\n## Key Advantages of dnd-kit\n\n**Framework Agnostic \u0026 Lightweight:**\ndnd-kit's core is only ~11KB gzipped with zero dependencies, and you install only what you need through modular packages.[3][4]\n\n**Better Grid Support:**\nreact-beautiful-dnd has known limitations with horizontal and vertical grid reordering,[4] whereas dnd-kit provides built-in grid support with examples like sortable image grids.[4]\n\n**Architecture:**\n- Separates concerns: sensors (mouse, touch, keyboard), collision detection, and context[3]\n- Uses DragOverlay portal for smooth animations without touching original DOM[3]\n- Framework-agnostic core with thin adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, and others[1][2]\n\n## Core Packages for Grid Portfolios\n\n- &#96;@dnd-kit/core&#96; - Core engine (~11KB)\n- &#96;@dnd-kit/sortable&#96; - Reorderable lists/grids (~3KB)\n- &#96;@dnd-kit/modifiers&#96; - Grid snapping, axis locking (~3.4KB)\n- &#96;@dnd-kit/utilities&#96; - Helper functions (~1.3KB)[4]\n\n## When to Use dnd-kit\n\ndnd-kit excels for portfolios needing flexible grid layouts with responsive sizing, variable item heights, and accessibility. It's more flexible and performant than react-beautiful-dnd for complex grid scenarios.[2][3][4]",

_**Agent (claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking)**_

Here’s how Nev Flynn’s portfolio grid and navbar animations are likely implemented, based on the [nev-clone](https://github.com/houssaineamzil/nev-clone) and public info about the original site.

---

## Tech stack

- **Next.js** + **React**
- **Framer Motion** for animations
- **react-grid-layout-next** for the draggable grid
- **styled-components** (original) or **SCSS** (clone)

---

## 1. Navbar / header animation

The header uses Framer Motion’s `useAnimation` for a fade-up on load:

```tsx
const controls = useAnimation();

useEffect(() => {
  controls.set({ y: 15, opacity: 0 });
  controls.start({
    y: 0,
    opacity: 1,
    transition: { duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" },
  });
}, []);

return (
  <motion.div
    initial={false}
    animate={controls}
    className={styles.header}
  >
    {/* Logo, filter, contact */}
  </motion.div>
);
```

The logo also re-triggers this animation on load via `onLoad`.

---

## 2. Grid layout and drag & drop

The grid is built with **react-grid-layout-next**:

- `ResponsiveGridLayout` with `WidthProvider` for responsive width
- Breakpoints for different screen sizes
- Each item has `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` in the layout config
- `isDraggable={true}` on desktop, disabled on touch devices

```tsx
<ResponsiveGridLayout
  layouts={layouts}
  breakpoints={{ lg: 1200, md: 800, sm: 375 }}
  cols={{ lg: 12, md: 8, sm: 4 }}
  onBreakpointChange={(breakpoint) => setHeight(heights[breakpoint])}
  margin={[16, 16]}
>
  {items.map((item) => (
    <div key={item.i} data-grid={item}>
      {/* Card content */}
    </div>
  ))}
</ResponsiveGridLayout>
```

---

## 3. Grid entrance animation

The grid container starts hidden and animates in:

- Initial state: `opacity: 0`, `will-change: transform, opacity`
- Page-level `motion.div` animates from `y: 15, opacity: 0` to `y: 0, opacity: 1`
- Grid items are shown after a short delay (e.g. 500ms) via `isMounted`

```scss
.GridContainer {
  opacity: 0;
  will-change: transform, opacity;
}
```

```tsx
// Page wraps everything in motion.div with same fade-up
<motion.div animate={controls} className={styles.container}>
  <Header ... />
  <motion.div className={cn(styles.GridContainer, isMounted && styles.visible)}>
    <Grid ... />
  </motion.div>
</motion.div>
```

---

## 4. Grid item styling

Grid items use CSS transitions for layout changes and hover:

```scss
.itemGrab {
  overflow: hidden;
  border-radius: 32px;
  user-select: none;
  &:hover { cursor: grab; }
  &:active { cursor: grabbing; }
}

.Item {
  transition: 0.25s ease;
  &:hover {
    box-shadow: rgba(100, 100, 111, 0.1) 0px 5px 24px 0px;
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Filter animation

When filtering, non-matching items fade:

```tsx
const opacityValue = (section) =>
  filter === "all" || section === filter ? 1 : 0.25;

// Applied to each grid item
style={{ opacity: opacityValue(item.section) }}
```

---

## Summary

| Element | Technique |
|--------|-----------|
| **Navbar** | Framer Motion `useAnimation` → `y: 15→0`, `opacity: 0→1` |
| **Grid layout** | `react-grid-layout-next` with responsive breakpoints |
| **Drag & drop** | Built into `react-grid-layout-next` |
| **Grid entrance** | Page-level `motion.div` + delayed `opacity` for items |
| **Item transitions** | CSS `transition` for layout and hover |
| **Filter** | Dynamic `opacity` on items based on filter state |

For your portfolio, you can mirror this with **Motion** (Framer Motion) for the header and grid entrance, and either **react-grid-layout** or **@dnd-kit** for the draggable bento grid.

---

The workaround is to either:\n- Set &#96;measureBeforeMount: false&#96; (accepts brief resize on first render)\n- Use the v2 API with &#96;useContainerWidth&#96; hook\n\nThe newer v2 architecture with TypeScript support and composable configuration is better suited for modern Next.js applications with SSR.[3][4]",

{
  "markdown": "# react-grid-layout v2.2.2\n\nA draggable and resizable grid layout with responsive breakpoints, for React.\n\n- Version: 2.2.2\n- Homepage: https://github.com/react-grid-layout/react-grid-layout\n- Repository: git+ssh://git@github.com/STRML/react-grid-layout.git\n- Author: Samuel Reed \n- Bugs: https://github.com/react-grid-layout/react-grid-layout/issues\n- Keywords: react, grid, drag, draggable, resize, resizable, fluid, responsive\n- License: MIT\n- Maintainers: strml \n- Weekly Downloads: 1.7M\n- Dependents: 830\n\n---\n\n# React-Grid-Layout\n\n[![npm package](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react-grid-layout.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.org/package/react-grid-layout)\n[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/react-grid-layout.svg?maxAge=2592000)]()\n\nReact-Grid-Layout is a grid layout system much like [Packery](http://packery.metafizzy.co/) or\n[Gridster](http://dsmorse.github.io/gridster.js/), for React.\n\nUnlike those systems, it is responsive and supports breakpoints. Breakpoint layouts can be provided by the user\nor autogenerated.\n\nRGL is React-only and does not require jQuery.\n\n![BitMEX UI](http://i.imgur.com/oo1NT6c.gif)\n\n\u003e GIF from production usage on [BitMEX.com](https://www.bitmex.com)\n\n[**[Demo](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/) | [Changelog](/CHANGELOG.md) | [CodeSandbox Editable demo](https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/5ywf7c)**]\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [What's New in v2](#whats-new-in-v2)\n- [Migrating from v1](#migrating-from-v1)\n- [Demos](#demos)\n- [Features](#features)\n- [Installation](#installation)\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Responsive Usage](#responsive-usage)\n- [Providing Grid Width](#providing-grid-width)\n- [Hooks API](#hooks-api)\n- [API Reference](#api-reference)\n- [Extending: Custom Compactors \u0026 Position Strategies](#extending-custom-compactors--position-strategies)\n- [Extras](#extras)\n- [Performance](#performance)\n- [Contribute](#contribute)\n\n## What's New in v2\n\nVersion 2 is a complete TypeScript rewrite with a modernized API:\n\n- **Full TypeScript support** - First-class types, no more &#96;@types/react-grid-layout&#96;\n- **React Hooks** - New &#96;useContainerWidth&#96;, &#96;useGridLayout&#96;, and &#96;useResponsiveLayout&#96; hooks\n- **Composable Configuration** - Group related props into focused interfaces:\n\n- &#96;gridConfig&#96; - cols, rowHeight, margin, padding\n - &#96;dragConfig&#96; - enable, handle, cancel, bounded\n - &#96;resizeConfig&#96; - enable, handles\n - &#96;positionStrategy&#96; - transform vs absolute positioning\n - &#96;compactor&#96; - vertical, horizontal, or custom algorithms\n\n- **Modular architecture** - Import only what you need:\n\n- &#96;react-grid-layout&#96; - React components and hooks (v2 API)\n - &#96;react-grid-layout/core&#96; - Pure layout algorithms (framework-agnostic)\n - &#96;react-grid-layout/legacy&#96; - v1 flat props API for migration\n - &#96;react-grid-layout/extras&#96; - Optional components like &#96;GridBackground&#96;\n\n- **Smaller bundle** - Tree-shakeable ESM and CJS builds\n\n### Breaking Changes\n\nSee the [RFC](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#breaking-changes-in-v2) for detailed migration examples.\n\n| Change | Description |\n| --- | --- |\n| [&#96;width&#96; prop required](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#breaking-changes-in-v2) | Use &#96;useContainerWidth&#96; hook or provide your own measurement |\n| [&#96;onDragStart&#96; threshold](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#1-ondragstart-no-longer-fires-on-click-only-events) | Now fires after 3px movement, not on mousedown. Use &#96;onMouseDown&#96; for immediate response |\n| [Immutable callbacks](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#2-immutable-callback-parameters) | Callback parameters are read-only. Use &#96;onLayoutChange&#96; or constraints instead of mutation |\n| [&#96;data-grid&#96; in legacy only](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#3-data-grid-prop-only-available-in-legacy-wrapper) | v2 requires explicit &#96;layout&#96; prop. Use legacy wrapper for &#96;data-grid&#96; |\n| [Pluggable compaction](./rfcs/0001-v2-typescript-rewrite.md#4-pluggable-compaction-algorithms) | Compaction is now pluggable via &#96;Compactor&#96; interface. Optional fast O(n log n) algorithm in &#96;/extras&#96; |\n| UMD bundle removed | Use a bundler (Vite, webpack, esbuild) |\n| &#96;verticalCompact&#96; removed | Use &#96;compactType={null}&#96; or &#96;compactor={noCompactor}&#96; |\n\n## Migrating from v1\n\n**Quick migration** - change your import to use the legacy wrapper:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;diff\n- import GridLayout, { Responsive, WidthProvider } from 'react-grid-layout';\n+ import GridLayout, { Responsive, WidthProvider } from 'react-grid-layout/legacy';\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis provides **100% runtime API compatibility** with v1.\n\n**TypeScript users**: If you were using &#96;@types/react-grid-layout&#96;, note that v2 includes its own types with some naming changes:\n\n| Old (&#96;@types/react-grid-layout&#96;) | New (v2) | Notes |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;RGL.Layout&#96; | &#96;LayoutItem&#96; | Single grid item |\n| &#96;RGL.Layout[]&#96; | &#96;Layout&#96; | Array of items |\n| &#96;RGL.Layouts&#96; | &#96;ResponsiveLayouts&#96; | Breakpoint → layout map |\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;diff\n- import RGL from 'react-grid-layout';\n- const item: RGL.Layout = { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 1 };\n- const layouts: RGL.Layouts = { lg: [item] };\n+ import { LayoutItem, ResponsiveLayouts } from 'react-grid-layout/legacy';\n+ const item: LayoutItem = { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 1 };\n+ const layouts: ResponsiveLayouts = { lg: [item] };\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Full migration** - adopt the v2 API for new features and better tree-shaking:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport ReactGridLayout, { useContainerWidth, verticalCompactor } from 'react-grid-layout';\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 (\n        \u003cReactGridLayout\n          width={width}\n          layout={layout}\n          gridConfig={{ cols: 12, rowHeight: 30 }}\n          dragConfig={{ enabled: true, handle: '.handle' }}\n          compactor={verticalCompactor}\n        \u003e\n          {children}\n        \u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n      )}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n| Use Case | Recommendation |\n| --- | --- |\n| Existing v1 codebase | &#96;react-grid-layout/legacy&#96; |\n| New project | v2 API with hooks |\n| Custom compaction | v2 with custom &#96;Compactor&#96; |\n| SSR | v2 with &#96;measureBeforeMount: true&#96; |\n\n## Demos\n\n1. [Showcase](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/00-showcase.html)\n2. [Basic](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/01-basic.html)\n3. [No Dragging/Resizing (Layout Only)](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/02-no-dragging.html)\n4. [Messy Layout Autocorrect](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/03-messy.html)\n5. [Layout Defined on Children](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/04-grid-property.html)\n6. [Static Elements](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/05-static-elements.html)\n7. [Adding/Removing Elements](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/06-dynamic-add-remove.html)\n8. [Saving a Responsive Layout to LocalStorage](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/08-localstorage-responsive.html)\n10. [Minimum and Maximum Width/Height](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/09-min-max-wh.html)\n11. [Dynamic Minimum and Maximum Width/Height](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/10-dynamic-min-max-wh.html)\n12. [Toolbox](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/11-toolbox.html)\n13. [Drag From Outside](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/12-drag-from-outside.html)\n14. [Responsive Bootstrap-style Layout](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/14-responsive-bootstrap-style.html)\n16. [Custom Constraints](https://react-grid-layout.github.io/react-grid-layout/examples/21-custom-constraints.html)\n\n#### Projects Using React-Grid-Layout\n\n- [Basedash](https://www.basedash.com)\n- [BitMEX](https://www.bitmex.com/)\n- [AWS CloudFront Dashboards](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/cloudwatch-dashboards-create-use-customized-metrics-views/)\n- [Grafana](https://grafana.com/)\n- [Metabase](http://www.metabase.com/)\n- [HubSpot](http://www.hubspot.com)\n- [Kibana](https://www.elastic.co/products/kibana)\n- [Monday](https://support.monday.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002187819-What-are-the-Dashboards-)\n\n_Know of others? Create a PR to let me know!_\n\n## Features\n\n- 100% React - no jQuery\n- Full TypeScript support\n- Compatible with server-rendered apps\n- Draggable widgets\n- Resizable widgets\n- Static widgets\n- Configurable packing: horizontal, vertical, or off\n- Bounds checking for dragging and resizing\n- Widgets may be added or removed without rebuilding grid\n- Layout can be serialized and restored\n- Responsive breakpoints\n- Separate layouts per responsive breakpoint\n- Grid Items placed using CSS Transforms\n- Compatibility with &#96; &#96;\n\n| Version | Compatibility |\n| --- | --- |\n| \u003e= 2.0.0 | React 18+, TypeScript |\n| \u003e= 0.17.0 | React 16 \u0026 17 |\n\n## Installation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install react-grid-layout\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nInclude the stylesheets in your application:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport \"react-grid-layout/css/styles.css\";\nimport \"react-resizable/css/styles.css\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr link them directly:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n\u003clink rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"/node_modules/react-grid-layout/css/styles.css\" /\u003e\n\u003clink rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"/node_modules/react-resizable/css/styles.css\" /\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Quick Start\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport ReactGridLayout, { useContainerWidth } from \"react-grid-layout\";\nimport \"react-grid-layout/css/styles.css\";\nimport \"react-resizable/css/styles.css\";\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  const layout = [\n    { i: \"a\", x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 2, static: true },\n    { i: \"b\", x: 1, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2, minW: 2, maxW: 4 },\n    { i: \"c\", x: 4, y: 0, w: 1, h: 2 }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 (\n        \u003cReactGridLayout\n          layout={layout}\n          width={width}\n          gridConfig={{ cols: 12, rowHeight: 30 }}\n        \u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"a\"\u003ea\u003c/div\u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"b\"\u003eb\u003c/div\u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"c\"\u003ec\u003c/div\u003e\n        \u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n      )}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can also define layout on children using &#96;data-grid&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n\u003cReactGridLayout width={width} gridConfig={{ cols: 12, rowHeight: 30 }}\u003e\n  \u003cdiv key=\"a\" data-grid={{ x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 2, static: true }}\u003e\n    a\n  \u003c/div\u003e\n  \u003cdiv key=\"b\" data-grid={{ x: 1, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2 }}\u003e\n    b\n  \u003c/div\u003e\n  \u003cdiv key=\"c\" data-grid={{ x: 4, y: 0, w: 1, h: 2 }}\u003e\n    c\n  \u003c/div\u003e\n\u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Responsive Usage\n\nUse &#96;Responsive&#96; for automatic breakpoint handling:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { Responsive, useContainerWidth } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction MyResponsiveGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  const layouts = {\n    lg: [{ i: \"1\", x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 }],\n    md: [{ i: \"1\", x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 }]\n  };\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 (\n        \u003cResponsive\n          layouts={layouts}\n          breakpoints={{ lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0 }}\n          cols={{ lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4, xxs: 2 }}\n          width={width}\n        \u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"1\"\u003e1\u003c/div\u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"2\"\u003e2\u003c/div\u003e\n          \u003cdiv key=\"3\"\u003e3\u003c/div\u003e\n        \u003c/Responsive\u003e\n      )}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Providing Grid Width\n\nThe &#96;width&#96; prop is required. You have several options:\n\n### Option 1: useContainerWidth Hook (Recommended)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport ReactGridLayout, { useContainerWidth } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 \u003cReactGridLayout width={width}\u003e...\u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option 2: Fixed Width\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n\u003cReactGridLayout width={1200}\u003e...\u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Option 3: CSS Container Queries or ResizeObserver\n\nUse any width measurement library like [react-sizeme](https://github.com/ctrlplusb/react-sizeme) or your own ResizeObserver implementation.\n\n### Option 4: Legacy WidthProvider HOC\n\nFor backwards compatibility, you can still use &#96;WidthProvider&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport ReactGridLayout, { WidthProvider } from \"react-grid-layout/legacy\";\n\nconst GridLayoutWithWidth = WidthProvider(ReactGridLayout);\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  return \u003cGridLayoutWithWidth\u003e...\u003c/GridLayoutWithWidth\u003e;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Hooks API\n\nThe v2 API provides three hooks for different use cases. Choose based on your needs:\n\n| Hook | Use When |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;useContainerWidth&#96; | You need responsive width measurement (most common) |\n| &#96;useGridLayout&#96; | You're building a custom grid component or need direct state control |\n| &#96;useResponsiveLayout&#96; | You're building a custom responsive grid with breakpoint logic |\n\n### useContainerWidth\n\nObserves container width using ResizeObserver and provides reactive width updates. This is the recommended way to provide width to the grid.\n\n**Why use it instead of WidthProvider?**\n\n- Hooks are more composable and easier to test\n- No HOC wrapper means simpler component tree\n- Explicit control over when to render (via &#96;mounted&#96;)\n- Works better with SSR\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useContainerWidth } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted, measureWidth } = useContainerWidth({\n    measureBeforeMount: false, // Set true for SSR\n    initialWidth: 1280 // Width before first measurement\n  });\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e{mounted \u0026\u0026 \u003cReactGridLayout width={width} /\u003e}\u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Type Definitions:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface UseContainerWidthOptions {\n  /** Delay render until width is measured. Useful for SSR. Default: false */\n  measureBeforeMount?: boolean;\n  /** Initial width before measurement. Default: 1280 */\n  initialWidth?: number;\n}\n\ninterface UseContainerWidthResult {\n  /** Current container width in pixels */\n  width: number;\n  /** Whether the container has been measured at least once */\n  mounted: boolean;\n  /** Ref to attach to the container element */\n  containerRef: RefObject\u003cHTMLDivElement | null\u003e;\n  /** Manually trigger a width measurement */\n  measureWidth: () =\u003e void;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### useGridLayout\n\nCore layout state management hook. Use this when you need direct control over drag/resize/drop state, or when building a custom grid component.\n\n**Why use it instead of the component?**\n\n- Full control over layout state and updates\n- Access to drag/resize/drop state for custom UIs\n- Can integrate with external state management\n- Build headless grid implementations\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useGridLayout, horizontalCompactor } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction CustomGrid({ initialLayout }) {\n  const {\n    layout,\n    setLayout,\n    dragState,\n    resizeState,\n    onDragStart,\n    onDrag,\n    onDragStop,\n    onResizeStart,\n    onResize,\n    onResizeStop,\n    containerHeight,\n    isInteracting,\n    compactor\n  } = useGridLayout({\n    layout: initialLayout,\n    cols: 12,\n    compactor: horizontalCompactor, // default is verticalCompactor\n    onLayoutChange: newLayout =\u003e console.log(\"Layout changed:\", newLayout)\n  });\n\n  // Access drag state for custom placeholder rendering\n  const placeholder = dragState.activeDrag;\n\n  // Check if any interaction is happening\n  if (isInteracting) {\n    // Disable other UI during drag/resize\n  }\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv style={{ height: containerHeight * rowHeight }}\u003e\n      {layout.map(item =\u003e (\n        \u003cdiv\n          key={item.i}\n          onMouseDown={() =\u003e onDragStart(item.i, item.x, item.y)}\n        \u003e\n          {item.i}\n        \u003c/div\u003e\n      ))}\n      {placeholder \u0026\u0026 \u003cdiv className=\"placeholder\" /\u003e}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Type Definitions:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface UseGridLayoutOptions {\n  /** Initial layout */\n  layout: Layout;\n  /** Number of columns */\n  cols: number;\n  /** Block movement into occupied space instead of pushing items */\n  preventCollision?: boolean;\n  /** Called when layout changes */\n  onLayoutChange?: (layout: Layout) =\u003e void;\n  /** Compactor for layout compaction (default: verticalCompactor) */\n  compactor?: Compactor;\n}\n\ninterface UseGridLayoutResult {\n  /** Current layout */\n  layout: Layout;\n  /** Set layout directly */\n  setLayout: (layout: Layout) =\u003e void;\n  /** Current drag state (activeDrag, oldDragItem, oldLayout) */\n  dragState: DragState;\n  /** Current resize state (resizing, oldResizeItem, oldLayout) */\n  resizeState: ResizeState;\n  /** Current drop state (droppingDOMNode, droppingPosition) */\n  dropState: DropState;\n  /** Start dragging an item */\n  onDragStart: (itemId: string, x: number, y: number) =\u003e LayoutItem | null;\n  /** Update drag position */\n  onDrag: (itemId: string, x: number, y: number) =\u003e void;\n  /** Stop dragging */\n  onDragStop: (itemId: string, x: number, y: number) =\u003e void;\n  /** Start resizing an item */\n  onResizeStart: (itemId: string) =\u003e LayoutItem | null;\n  /** Update resize dimensions */\n  onResize: (\n    itemId: string,\n    w: number,\n    h: number,\n    x?: number,\n    y?: number\n  ) =\u003e void;\n  /** Stop resizing */\n  onResizeStop: (itemId: string, w: number, h: number) =\u003e void;\n  /** Handle external drag over */\n  onDropDragOver: (\n    droppingItem: LayoutItem,\n    position: DroppingPosition\n  ) =\u003e void;\n  /** Handle external drag leave */\n  onDropDragLeave: () =\u003e void;\n  /** Complete external drop */\n  onDrop: (droppingItem: LayoutItem) =\u003e void;\n  /** Container height in grid rows */\n  containerHeight: number;\n  /** Whether any drag/resize/drop is active */\n  isInteracting: boolean;\n  /** The compactor being used */\n  compactor: Compactor;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### useResponsiveLayout\n\nManages responsive breakpoints and generates layouts for different screen sizes. Use this when building a custom responsive grid.\n\n**Why use it instead of the Responsive component?**\n\n- Direct access to current breakpoint\n- Control over layout generation for new breakpoints\n- Can update layouts for specific breakpoints\n- Build custom breakpoint UIs\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { useContainerWidth, useResponsiveLayout } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction CustomResponsiveGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  const {\n    layout, // Current layout for active breakpoint\n    layouts, // All layouts by breakpoint\n    breakpoint, // Current active breakpoint ('lg', 'md', etc.)\n    cols, // Column count for current breakpoint\n    setLayoutForBreakpoint,\n    setLayouts,\n    sortedBreakpoints\n  } = useResponsiveLayout({\n    width,\n    breakpoints: { lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0 },\n    cols: { lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4, xxs: 2 },\n    layouts: {\n      lg: [{ i: \"1\", x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 }],\n      md: [{ i: \"1\", x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2 }]\n    },\n    // compactor: verticalCompactor (default)\n    onBreakpointChange: (bp, cols) =\u003e\n      console.log(&#96;Now at ${bp} (${cols} cols)&#96;),\n    onLayoutChange: (layout, allLayouts) =\u003e saveToServer(allLayouts)\n  });\n\n  // Show current breakpoint in UI\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef}\u003e\n      \u003cdiv\u003e\n        Current breakpoint: {breakpoint} ({cols} columns)\n      \u003c/div\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 (\n        \u003cGridLayout width={width} cols={cols} layout={layout}\u003e\n          {/* children */}\n        \u003c/GridLayout\u003e\n      )}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Type Definitions:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface UseResponsiveLayoutOptions\u003cB extends string = DefaultBreakpoints\u003e {\n  /** Current container width */\n  width: number;\n  /** Breakpoint definitions (name → min-width). Default: {lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0} */\n  breakpoints?: Record\u003cB, number\u003e;\n  /** Column counts per breakpoint. Default: {lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4, xxs: 2} */\n  cols?: Record\u003cB, number\u003e;\n  /** Layouts for each breakpoint */\n  layouts?: Partial\u003cRecord\u003cB, Layout\u003e\u003e;\n  /** Compactor for layout compaction (default: verticalCompactor) */\n  compactor?: Compactor;\n  /** Called when breakpoint changes */\n  onBreakpointChange?: (newBreakpoint: B, cols: number) =\u003e void;\n  /** Called when layout changes */\n  onLayoutChange?: (layout: Layout, layouts: Record\u003cB, Layout\u003e) =\u003e void;\n  /** Called when width changes */\n  onWidthChange?: (\n    width: number,\n    margin: [number, number],\n    cols: number,\n    padding: [number, number] | null\n  ) =\u003e void;\n}\n\ninterface UseResponsiveLayoutResult\u003cB extends string = DefaultBreakpoints\u003e {\n  /** Current layout for the active breakpoint */\n  layout: Layout;\n  /** All layouts by breakpoint */\n  layouts: Partial\u003cRecord\u003cB, Layout\u003e\u003e;\n  /** Current active breakpoint */\n  breakpoint: B;\n  /** Column count for the current breakpoint */\n  cols: number;\n  /** Update layout for a specific breakpoint */\n  setLayoutForBreakpoint: (breakpoint: B, layout: Layout) =\u003e void;\n  /** Update all layouts */\n  setLayouts: (layouts: Partial\u003cRecord\u003cB, Layout\u003e\u003e) =\u003e void;\n  /** Sorted array of breakpoint names (smallest to largest) */\n  sortedBreakpoints: B[];\n}\n\ntype DefaultBreakpoints = \"lg\" | \"md\" | \"sm\" | \"xs\" | \"xxs\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## API Reference\n\n### ReactGridLayout Props\n\nThe v2 API uses composable configuration interfaces for cleaner prop organization:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface ReactGridLayoutProps {\n  // Required\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n  width: number; // Container width in pixels\n\n  // Configuration interfaces (see below for details)\n  gridConfig?: Partial\u003cGridConfig\u003e; // Grid measurement settings\n  dragConfig?: Partial\u003cDragConfig\u003e; // Drag behavior settings\n  resizeConfig?: Partial\u003cResizeConfig\u003e; // Resize behavior settings\n  dropConfig?: Partial\u003cDropConfig\u003e; // External drop settings\n  positionStrategy?: PositionStrategy; // CSS positioning strategy\n  compactor?: Compactor; // Layout compaction strategy\n\n  // Layout data\n  layout?: Layout; // Layout definition\n  droppingItem?: LayoutItem; // Item configuration when dropping from outside\n\n  // Container\n  autoSize?: boolean; // Auto-size container height (default: true)\n  className?: string;\n  style?: React.CSSProperties;\n  innerRef?: React.Ref\u003cHTMLDivElement\u003e;\n\n  // Callbacks\n  onLayoutChange?: (layout: Layout) =\u003e void;\n  onDragStart?: EventCallback;\n  onDrag?: EventCallback;\n  onDragStop?: EventCallback;\n  onResizeStart?: EventCallback;\n  onResize?: EventCallback;\n  onResizeStop?: EventCallback;\n  onDrop?: (layout: Layout, item: LayoutItem | undefined, e: Event) =\u003e void;\n  onDropDragOver?: (e: DragEvent) =\u003e { w?: number; h?: number } | false | void;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### GridConfig\n\nGrid measurement configuration:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface GridConfig {\n  cols: number; // Number of columns (default: 12)\n  rowHeight: number; // Row height in pixels (default: 150)\n  margin: [number, number]; // [x, y] margin between items (default: [10, 10])\n  containerPadding: [number, number] | null; // Container padding (default: null, uses margin)\n  maxRows: number; // Maximum rows (default: Infinity)\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### DragConfig\n\nDrag behavior configuration:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface DragConfig {\n  enabled: boolean; // Enable dragging (default: true)\n  bounded: boolean; // Keep items within container (default: false)\n  handle?: string; // CSS selector for drag handle\n  cancel?: string; // CSS selector to cancel dragging\n  threshold: number; // Pixels to move before drag starts (default: 3)\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### ResizeConfig\n\nResize behavior configuration:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface ResizeConfig {\n  enabled: boolean; // Enable resizing (default: true)\n  handles: ResizeHandleAxis[]; // Handle positions (default: ['se'])\n  handleComponent?: React.ReactNode | ((axis, ref) =\u003e React.ReactNode);\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### DropConfig\n\nExternal drop configuration:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface DropConfig {\n  enabled: boolean; // Allow external drops (default: false)\n  defaultItem: { w: number; h: number }; // Default size (default: { w: 1, h: 1 })\n  onDragOver?: (e: DragEvent) =\u003e { w?: number; h?: number } | false | void;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### PositionStrategy\n\nCSS positioning strategy. Built-in options:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport {\n  transformStrategy, // Default: use CSS transforms\n  absoluteStrategy, // Use top/left positioning\n  createScaledStrategy // For scaled containers\n} from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n\n// Example: scaled container\n\u003cdiv style={{ transform: 'scale(0.5)' }}\u003e\n  \u003cReactGridLayout positionStrategy={createScaledStrategy(0.5)} ... /\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Compactor\n\nLayout compaction strategy. Built-in options:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport {\n  verticalCompactor, // Default: compact items upward\n  horizontalCompactor, // Compact items leftward\n  noCompactor, // No compaction (free positioning)\n  getCompactor // Factory: getCompactor('vertical', allowOverlap, preventCollision)\n} from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### ResponsiveGridLayout Props\n\nExtends &#96;GridLayoutProps&#96; with responsive-specific props:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface ResponsiveGridLayoutProps\u003cB extends string = string\u003e {\n  // Responsive configuration\n  breakpoint?: B; // Current breakpoint (auto-detected)\n  breakpoints?: Record\u003cB, number\u003e; // Breakpoint definitions (default: {lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0})\n  cols?: Record\u003cB, number\u003e; // Columns per breakpoint (default: {lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4, xxs: 2})\n  layouts?: Record\u003cB, Layout\u003e; // Layouts per breakpoint\n\n  // Can be fixed or per-breakpoint\n  margin?: [number, number] | Partial\u003cRecord\u003cB, [number, number]\u003e\u003e;\n  containerPadding?:\n    | [number, number]\n    | Partial\u003cRecord\u003cB, [number, number] | null\u003e\u003e\n    | null;\n\n  // Callbacks\n  onBreakpointChange?: (newBreakpoint: B, cols: number) =\u003e void;\n  onLayoutChange?: (layout: Layout, layouts: Record\u003cB, Layout\u003e) =\u003e void;\n  onWidthChange?: (\n    width: number,\n    margin: [number, number],\n    cols: number,\n    padding: [number, number] | null\n  ) =\u003e void;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Layout Item\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface LayoutItem {\n  i: string; // Unique identifier (must match child key)\n  x: number; // X position in grid units\n  y: number; // Y position in grid units\n  w: number; // Width in grid units\n  h: number; // Height in grid units\n  minW?: number; // Minimum width (default: 0)\n  maxW?: number; // Maximum width (default: Infinity)\n  minH?: number; // Minimum height (default: 0)\n  maxH?: number; // Maximum height (default: Infinity)\n  static?: boolean; // If true, not draggable or resizable\n  isDraggable?: boolean; // Override grid isDraggable\n  isResizable?: boolean; // Override grid isResizable\n  isBounded?: boolean; // Override grid isBounded\n  resizeHandles?: Array\u003c\"s\" | \"w\" | \"e\" | \"n\" | \"sw\" | \"nw\" | \"se\" | \"ne\"\u003e;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Core Utilities\n\nImport pure layout functions from &#96;react-grid-layout/core&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport {\n  verticalCompactor,\n  horizontalCompactor,\n  noCompactor,\n  getCompactor,\n  moveElement,\n  collides,\n  getFirstCollision,\n  validateLayout\n  // ... and more\n} from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e **Note**: The &#96;compact()&#96; function is not exported. Use compactors instead: &#96;verticalCompactor.compact(layout, cols)&#96; or get one via &#96;getCompactor('vertical')&#96;.\n\n## Extending: Custom Compactors \u0026 Position Strategies\n\n### Creating a Custom Compactor\n\nCompactors control how items are arranged after drag/resize. Create your own for custom layouts like masonry, gravity, or shelf-packing.\n\n**The Compactor Interface:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface Compactor {\n  /** Identifies the compaction type */\n  type: \"vertical\" | \"horizontal\" | null | string;\n\n  /**\n   * Whether items can overlap each other.\n   *\n   * When true:\n   * - Items can be placed on top of other items\n   * - Dragging into another item does NOT push it away\n   * - Compaction is skipped after drag/resize\n   *\n   * Use for: layered dashboards, free-form layouts\n   */\n  allowOverlap: boolean;\n\n  /**\n   * Whether to block movement that would cause collision.\n   *\n   * When true (and allowOverlap is false):\n   * - Dragging into another item is blocked (item snaps back)\n   * - Other items are NOT pushed away\n   * - Only affects movement, not compaction\n   *\n   * Use with noCompactor for: fixed grids, slot-based layouts\n   *\n   * Note: Has no effect when allowOverlap is true.\n   */\n  preventCollision?: boolean;\n\n  /**\n   * Compact the entire layout.\n   * Called after any layout change to fill gaps.\n   *\n   * @param layout - Array of layout items (clone before mutating!)\n   * @param cols - Number of grid columns\n   * @returns New compacted layout\n   */\n  compact(layout: Layout, cols: number): Layout;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example: Gravity Compactor (items fall to bottom)**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { cloneLayout, cloneLayoutItem, getStatics, bottom } from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n\nconst gravityCompactor: Compactor = {\n  type: \"gravity\",\n  allowOverlap: false,\n\n  compact(layout, cols) {\n    const statics = getStatics(layout);\n    const maxY = 100; // arbitrary max height\n    const out = [];\n\n    // Sort by Y descending (process bottom items first)\n    const sorted = [...layout].sort((a, b) =\u003e b.y - a.y);\n\n    for (const item of sorted) {\n      const l = cloneLayoutItem(item);\n\n      if (!l.static) {\n        // Move down as far as possible\n        while (l.y \u003c maxY \u0026\u0026 !collides(l, statics)) {\n          l.y++;\n        }\n        l.y--; // Back up one\n      }\n\n      out.push(l);\n    }\n\n    return out;\n  }\n};\n\n// Usage\n\u003cGridLayout compactor={gravityCompactor} /\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example: Single Row Compactor (horizontal shelf)**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nconst singleRowCompactor: Compactor = {\n  type: \"shelf\",\n  allowOverlap: false,\n\n  compact(layout, cols) {\n    let x = 0;\n    const out = [];\n\n    // Sort by original X position\n    const sorted = [...layout].sort((a, b) =\u003e a.x - b.x);\n\n    for (const item of sorted) {\n      const l = cloneLayoutItem(item);\n      if (!l.static) {\n        l.x = x;\n        l.y = 0; // All items on row 0\n        x += l.w;\n\n        // Wrap to next row if overflow\n        if (x \u003e cols) {\n          l.x = 0;\n          x = l.w;\n        }\n      }\n      out.push(l);\n    }\n\n    return out;\n  }\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Using Helper Functions:**\n\nThe core module exports helpers for building compactors:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport {\n  resolveCompactionCollision, // Move items to resolve overlaps\n  compactItemVertical, // Compact one item upward\n  compactItemHorizontal, // Compact one item leftward\n  getFirstCollision, // Find first collision\n  collides, // Check if two items collide\n  getStatics, // Get static items from layout\n  cloneLayout, // Clone layout array\n  cloneLayoutItem // Clone single item\n} from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Creating a Custom Position Strategy\n\nPosition strategies control how items are positioned via CSS. Create custom strategies for special transform handling.\n\n**The PositionStrategy Interface:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface PositionStrategy {\n  /** Type identifier */\n  type: \"transform\" | \"absolute\" | string;\n\n  /** Scale factor for coordinate calculations */\n  scale: number;\n\n  /**\n   * Generate CSS styles for positioning an item.\n   *\n   * @param pos - Position with top, left, width, height in pixels\n   * @returns CSS properties object\n   */\n  calcStyle(pos: Position): React.CSSProperties;\n\n  /**\n   * Calculate drag position from mouse coordinates.\n   * Used during drag to convert screen coords to grid coords.\n   *\n   * @param clientX - Mouse X position\n   * @param clientY - Mouse Y position\n   * @param offsetX - Offset from item left edge\n   * @param offsetY - Offset from item top edge\n   * @returns Calculated left/top position\n   */\n  calcDragPosition(\n    clientX: number,\n    clientY: number,\n    offsetX: number,\n    offsetY: number\n  ): { left: number; top: number };\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example: Rotated Container Strategy**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nconst createRotatedStrategy = (angleDegrees: number): PositionStrategy =\u003e {\n  const angleRad = (angleDegrees * Math.PI) / 180;\n  const cos = Math.cos(angleRad);\n  const sin = Math.sin(angleRad);\n\n  return {\n    type: \"rotated\",\n    scale: 1,\n\n    calcStyle(pos) {\n      // Apply rotation to position\n      const rotatedX = pos.left * cos - pos.top * sin;\n      const rotatedY = pos.left * sin + pos.top * cos;\n\n      return {\n        transform: &#96;translate(${rotatedX}px, ${rotatedY}px)&#96;,\n        width: &#96;${pos.width}px&#96;,\n        height: &#96;${pos.height}px&#96;,\n        position: \"absolute\"\n      };\n    },\n\n    calcDragPosition(clientX, clientY, offsetX, offsetY) {\n      // Reverse the rotation for drag calculations\n      const x = clientX - offsetX;\n      const y = clientY - offsetY;\n\n      return {\n        left: x * cos + y * sin,\n        top: -x * sin + y * cos\n      };\n    }\n  };\n};\n\n// Usage: grid inside a rotated container\n\u003cdiv style={{ transform: 'rotate(45deg)' }}\u003e\n  \u003cGridLayout positionStrategy={createRotatedStrategy(45)} /\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example: 3D Perspective Strategy**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nconst create3DStrategy = (\n  perspective: number,\n  rotateX: number\n): PositionStrategy =\u003e ({\n  type: \"3d\",\n  scale: 1,\n\n  calcStyle(pos) {\n    return {\n      transform: &#96;\n        perspective(${perspective}px)\n        rotateX(${rotateX}deg)\n        translate3d(${pos.left}px, ${pos.top}px, 0)\n      &#96;,\n      width: &#96;${pos.width}px&#96;,\n      height: &#96;${pos.height}px&#96;,\n      position: \"absolute\",\n      transformStyle: \"preserve-3d\"\n    };\n  },\n\n  calcDragPosition(clientX, clientY, offsetX, offsetY) {\n    // Adjust for perspective foreshortening\n    const perspectiveFactor = 1 + clientY / perspective;\n    return {\n      left: (clientX - offsetX) / perspectiveFactor,\n      top: (clientY - offsetY) / perspectiveFactor\n    };\n  }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Extras\n\nThe &#96;react-grid-layout/extras&#96; entry point provides optional components that extend react-grid-layout. These are tree-shakeable and won't be included in your bundle unless explicitly imported.\n\n### GridBackground\n\nRenders an SVG grid background that aligns with GridLayout cells. Use this to visualize the grid structure behind your layout.\n\n\u003e Based on [PR #2175](https://github.com/react-grid-layout/react-grid-layout/pull/2175) by [@dmj900501](https://github.com/dmj900501).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { GridBackground } from \"react-grid-layout/extras\";\nimport ReactGridLayout, { useContainerWidth } from \"react-grid-layout\";\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth();\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv ref={containerRef} style={{ position: \"relative\" }}\u003e\n      {mounted \u0026\u0026 (\n        \u003c\u003e\n          \u003cGridBackground\n            width={width}\n            cols={12}\n            rowHeight={30}\n            margin={[10, 10]}\n            rows={10}\n            color=\"#f0f0f0\"\n            borderRadius={4}\n          /\u003e\n          \u003cReactGridLayout\n            width={width}\n            gridConfig={{ cols: 12, rowHeight: 30, margin: [10, 10] }}\n          \u003e\n            {children}\n          \u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n        \u003c/\u003e\n      )}\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Props:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\ninterface GridBackgroundProps {\n  // Required - must match your GridLayout config\n  width: number; // Container width\n  cols: number; // Number of columns\n  rowHeight: number; // Row height in pixels\n\n  // Optional\n  margin?: [number, number]; // Gap between cells (default: [10, 10])\n  containerPadding?: [number, number] | null; // Container padding (default: uses margin)\n  rows?: number | \"auto\"; // Number of rows to display (default: 10)\n  height?: number; // Used when rows=\"auto\" to calculate row count\n  color?: string; // Cell background color (default: \"#e0e0e0\")\n  borderRadius?: number; // Cell border radius (default: 4)\n  className?: string; // Additional CSS class\n  style?: React.CSSProperties; // Additional inline styles\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Fast Compactors\n\nFor large layouts (200+ items), the standard compactors can become slow due to O(n²) collision resolution. The fast compactors use optimized algorithms with O(n log n) complexity.\n\n\u003e Based on the \"rising tide\" algorithm from [PR #2152](https://github.com/react-grid-layout/react-grid-layout/pull/2152) by [@morris](https://github.com/morris).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport {\n  fastVerticalCompactor,\n  fastHorizontalCompactor,\n  fastVerticalOverlapCompactor,\n  fastHorizontalOverlapCompactor\n} from \"react-grid-layout/extras\";\n\n\u003cReactGridLayout\n  compactor={fastVerticalCompactor}\n  // or compactor={fastHorizontalCompactor}\n  layout={layout}\n  width={width}\n/\u003e;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Performance Benchmarks:**\n\n| Items | Standard Vertical | Fast Vertical | Speedup |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 50 | 112 µs | 19 µs | **6x** |\n| 100 | 203 µs | 36 µs | **6x** |\n| 200 | 821 µs | 51 µs | **16x** |\n| 500 | 5.7 ms | 129 µs | **45x** |\n\n| Items | Standard Horizontal | Fast Horizontal | Speedup |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 50 | 164 µs | 12 µs | **14x** |\n| 100 | 477 µs | 25 µs | **19x** |\n| 200 | 1.1 ms | 42 µs | **26x** |\n| 500 | 9.5 ms | 128 µs | **74x** |\n\n**Correctness:**\n\nThe fast compactors produce layouts identical to the standard compactors:\n\n- **Vertical**: 0% height difference on deterministic 100-item layouts\n- **Horizontal**: 0% width difference on deterministic 100-item layouts\n- Both pass all correctness tests: no overlaps, idempotent, static item handling\n\n**When to use:**\n\n- Use fast compactors for dashboards with 200+ widgets\n- For smaller layouts (\u003c100 items), standard compactors work equally well\n- Both standard and fast compactors produce valid, non-overlapping layouts\n\n### calcGridCellDimensions (Core Utility)\n\nFor building custom grid overlays or backgrounds, use the &#96;calcGridCellDimensions&#96; utility from &#96;react-grid-layout/core&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { calcGridCellDimensions } from \"react-grid-layout/core\";\n\nconst dims = calcGridCellDimensions({\n  width: 1200,\n  cols: 12,\n  rowHeight: 30,\n  margin: [10, 10],\n  containerPadding: [20, 20]\n});\n\n// dims = {\n//   cellWidth: 88.33,  // Width of each cell\n//   cellHeight: 30,     // Height of each cell (= rowHeight)\n//   offsetX: 20,        // Left padding\n//   offsetY: 20,        // Top padding\n//   gapX: 10,           // Horizontal gap between cells\n//   gapY: 10,           // Vertical gap between cells\n//   cols: 12,           // Column count\n//   containerWidth: 1200\n// }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis is useful for building custom visualizations, snap-to-grid functionality, or integrating with canvas/WebGL renderers.\n\n## Performance\n\n### Memoize Children\n\nThe grid compares children by reference. Memoize them for better performance:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nfunction MyGrid({ count, width }) {\n  const children = useMemo(() =\u003e {\n    return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) =\u003e (\n      \u003cdiv\n        key={i}\n        data-grid={{ x: i % 12, y: Math.floor(i / 12), w: 1, h: 1 }}\n      /\u003e\n    ));\n  }, [count]);\n\n  return (\n    \u003cReactGridLayout width={width} gridConfig={{ cols: 12 }}\u003e\n      {children}\n    \u003c/ReactGridLayout\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Avoid Creating Components in Render (Legacy WidthProvider)\n\nIf using the legacy WidthProvider HOC, don't create the component during render:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport ReactGridLayout, { WidthProvider } from \"react-grid-layout/legacy\";\n\n// Bad - creates new component every render\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  const GridLayoutWithWidth = WidthProvider(ReactGridLayout);\n  return \u003cGridLayoutWithWidth\u003e...\u003c/GridLayoutWithWidth\u003e;\n}\n\n// Good - create once outside or with useMemo\nconst GridLayoutWithWidth = WidthProvider(ReactGridLayout);\n\nfunction MyGrid() {\n  return \u003cGridLayoutWithWidth\u003e...\u003c/GridLayoutWithWidth\u003e;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWith the v2 API, use &#96;useContainerWidth&#96; hook instead to avoid this issue entirely.\n\n## Custom Child Components\n\nGrid children must forward refs and certain props:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nconst CustomItem = forwardRef\u003cHTMLDivElement, CustomItemProps\u003e(\n  (\n    {\n      style,\n      className,\n      onMouseDown,\n      onMouseUp,\n      onTouchEnd,\n      children,\n      ...props\n    },\n    ref\n  ) =\u003e {\n    return (\n      \u003cdiv\n        ref={ref}\n        style={style}\n        className={className}\n        onMouseDown={onMouseDown}\n        onMouseUp={onMouseUp}\n        onTouchEnd={onTouchEnd}\n      \u003e\n        {children}\n Comparison of alternatives and how they fit your stack:

---

## 1. **react-grid-layout** (official) — recommended

The main [react-grid-layout](https://github.com/react-grid-layout/react-grid-layout) package is actively maintained (v2.2.2, Dec 2025) and works well with Next.js.

### Next.js / SSR

- **`useContainerWidth`** – measures container width on the client and avoids layout issues during SSR.
- **`measureBeforeMount`** – optional delay until width is measured (useful for SSR).
- **`mounted`** – lets you render the grid only after measurement to avoid hydration issues.

```tsx
import ReactGridLayout, { useContainerWidth } from "react-grid-layout";
import "react-grid-layout/css/styles.css";
import "react-resizable/css/styles.css";

function BentoGrid() {
  const { width, containerRef, mounted } = useContainerWidth({
    measureBeforeMount: true, // For SSR
    initialWidth: 1280,
  });

  return (
    <div ref={containerRef}>
      {mounted && (
        <ReactGridLayout
          width={width}
          layout={layout}
          gridConfig={{ cols: 12, rowHeight: 30, margin: [16, 16] }}
        >
          {/* children */}
        </ReactGridLayout>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Compatibility with your stack

- **React 19** – peer deps allow `>= 16.3.0`, so React 19 is supported.
- **Next.js 16** – works with App Router; use a client component (`"use client"`) because the grid needs `ResizeObserver` and DOM measurement.

### v2 features

- TypeScript
- Tree-shakeable ESM
- Hooks API (`useContainerWidth`, `useGridLayout`, `useResponsiveLayout`)
- Responsive breakpoints
- Optional resizing (can be disabled for a bento-style layout)

---

## 2. **@dnd-kit** — alternative for custom grids

[@dnd-kit](https://dndkit.com/) is a modern drag-and-drop library with sortable support. It’s more flexible but you build the grid layout yourself.

| Aspect | react-grid-layout | @dnd-kit |
|--------|-------------------|----------|
| Grid layout | Built-in (cols, rows, breakpoints) | You define layout (e.g. CSS Grid) |
| Variable cell sizes | Yes (w, h per item) | Yes (via your CSS) |
| Responsive | Built-in | Manual |
| Resizing | Built-in | Not included |
| Bundle size | ~30KB | ~11KB core |
| Best for | Dashboards, bento grids | Sortable lists, custom layouts |

For a Nev Flynn–style bento grid with fixed cell sizes and no resizing, either library works; `react-grid-layout` gives you layout and breakpoints out of the box.

---

## 3. **react-grid-layout-next** — avoid

- Last update ~3 years ago
- Superseded by official v2
- No clear advantage over the main package

---

## Recommendation for your portfolio

Use **react-grid-layout** v2:

1. Actively maintained
2. Designed for Next.js/SSR via `useContainerWidth` and `measureBeforeMount`
3. Compatible with React 19 and Next.js 16
4. Built-in responsive breakpoints and layout
5. Widely used (22k+ stars, 1.8M weekly downloads)

Install:

```bash
pnpm add react-grid-layout react-resizable
```

Then import the styles:

```ts
import "react-grid-layout/css/styles.css";
import "react-resizable/css/styles.css";
```

For a bento grid without resizing, set `resizeConfig={{ enabled: false }}` in the grid config.

for 'placeholder'.\n//\ntype ItemCallback = (layout: Layout, oldItem: LayoutItem, newItem: LayoutItem,\nplaceholder: LayoutItem, e: MouseEvent, element: HTMLElement) =\u003e void,\n\n// Calls when drag starts.\nonDragStart: ItemCallback,\n// Calls on each drag movement.\nonDrag: ItemCallback,\n// Calls when drag is complete.\nonDragStop: ItemCallback,\n// Calls when resize starts.\nonResizeStart: ItemCallback,\n// Calls when resize movement happens.\nonResize: ItemCallback,\n// Calls when resize is complete.\nonResizeStop: ItemCallback,\n\n//\n// Dropover functionality\n//\n\n// Calls when an element has been dropped into the grid from outside.\nonDrop: (layout: Layout, item?: LayoutItem, e: Event) =\u003e void,\n// Calls when an element is being dragged over the grid from outside as above.\n// This callback should return an object to dynamically change the droppingItem size\n// Return false to short-circuit the dragover\nonDropDragOver: (e: DragOverEvent) =\u003e ?({|w?: number, h?: number|} | false),\n\n// Ref for getting a reference for the grid's wrapping div.\n// You can use this instead of a regular ref and the deprecated &#96;ReactDOM.findDOMNode()&#96;&#96; function.\n// Note that this type is React.Ref in TypeScript, Flow has a bug here\n// https://github.com/facebook/flow/issues/8671#issuecomment-862634865\ninnerRef: {current: null | HTMLDivElement},\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Responsive Grid Layout Props\n\nThe responsive grid layout can be used instead. It supports all of the props above, excepting &#96;layout&#96;.\nThe new properties and changes are:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// {name: pxVal}, e.g. {lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480}\n// Breakpoint names are arbitrary but must match in the cols and layouts objects.\nbreakpoints?: Object = {lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0},\n\n// # of cols. Can be specified either as horizontal and vertical padding, e.g. &#96;[10, 10]&#96; or as a breakpoint -\u003e containerPadding map, e.g. &#96;{lg: [10, 10], md: [10, 10], ...}.\ncontainerPadding: [number, number] | {[breakpoint: $Keys]: [number, number]},\n\n// layouts is an object mapping breakpoints to layouts.\n// e.g. {lg: Layout, md: Layout, ...}\nlayouts: {[key: $Keys]: Layout},\n\n//\n// Callbacks\n//\n\n// Calls back with breakpoint and new # cols\nonBreakpointChange: (newBreakpoint: string, newCols: number) =\u003e void,\n\n// Callback so you can save the layout.\n// AllLayouts are keyed by breakpoint.\nonLayoutChange: (currentLayout: Layout, allLayouts: {[key: $Keys]: Layout}) =\u003e void,\n\n// Callback when the width changes, so you can modify the layout as needed.\nonWidthChange: (containerWidth: number, margin: [number, number], cols: number, containerPadding: [number, number]) =\u003e void;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Grid Item Props\n\nRGL supports the following properties on grid items or layout items. For\nexample, if the layout has the property &#96;isDraggable: false&#96;, but the grid item has the prop &#96;isDraggable: true&#96;, the item\nwill be draggable, even if the item is marked &#96;static: true&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n{\n\n// A string corresponding to the component key\ni: string,\n\n// These are all in grid units, not pixels\nx: number,\ny: number,\nw: number,\nh: number,\nminW?: number = 0,\nmaxW?: number = Infinity,\nminH?: number = 0,\nmaxH?: number = Infinity,\n\n// If true, equal to &#96;isDraggable: false, isResizable: false&#96;.\nstatic?: boolean = false,\n// If false, will not be draggable. Overrides &#96;static&#96;.\nisDraggable?: boolean = true,\n// If false, will not be resizable. Overrides &#96;static&#96;.\nisResizable?: boolean = true,\n// By default, a handle is only shown on the bottom-right (southeast) corner.\n// Note that resizing from the top or left is generally not intuitive.\nresizeHandles??: Array\u003c's' | 'w' | 'e' | 'n' | 'sw' | 'nw' | 'se' | 'ne'\u003e = ['se']\n// If true and draggable, item will be moved only within grid.\nisBounded?: boolean = false\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Grid Item Heights and Widths\n\nGrid item widths are based on container and number of columns. The size of a grid unit's height is based on &#96;rowHeight&#96;.\n\nNote that an item that has &#96;h=2&#96; is not exactly twice as tall as one with &#96;h=1&#96; unless you have no &#96;margin&#96;!\n\nIn order for the grid to not be ragged, when an item spans grid units, it must also span margins. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nfunction MyGrid(props) {\nconst children = React.useMemo(() =\u003e {\nreturn new Array(props.count).fill(undefined).map((val, idx) =\u003e {\nreturn ;\n});\n}, [props.count]);\nreturn {children};\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBecause the &#96;children&#96; prop doesn't change between rerenders, updates to &#96;&#96; won't result in new renders, improving performance.\n\n### React Hooks Performance\n\nUsing hooks to save your layout state on change will cause the layouts to re-render as the ResponsiveGridLayout will change it's value on every render.\nTo avoid this you should wrap your WidthProvider in a useMemo:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconst ResponsiveGridLayout = useMemo(() =\u003e WidthProvider(Responsive), []);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Custom Child Components and Draggable Handles\n\nIf you use React Components as grid children, they need to do a few things:\n\n- Forward refs to an underlying DOM node, and\n\n- Forward &#96;style&#96;,&#96;className&#96;, &#96;onMouseDown&#96;, &#96;onMouseUp&#96; and &#96;onTouchEnd&#96; to that same DOM node.\n\nFor example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconst CustomGridItemComponent = React.forwardRef(({style, className, onMouseDown, onMouseUp, onTouchEnd, children, ...props}, ref) =\u003e {\nreturn (\n\n{/* Some other content */}\n{children} {/* Make sure to include children to add resizable handle */}\n\n);\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe same is true of custom elements as draggable handles using the &#96;draggableHandle&#96; prop. This is so that\nthe underlying &#96;react-draggable&#96; library can get a reference to the DOM node underneath, manipulate\npositioning via &#96;style&#96;, and set classes.\n\n## Contribute\n\nIf you have a feature request, please add it as an issue or make a pull request.\n\nIf you have a bug to report, please reproduce the bug in [CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/s/staging-bush-3lvt7?file=/src/ShowcaseLayout.js) to help\nus easily isolate it.\n\n## TODO List\n\n- Basic grid layout\n\n- Fluid grid layout\n\n- Grid packing\n\n- Draggable grid items\n\n- Live grid packing while dragging\n\n- Resizable grid items\n\n- Layouts per responsive breakpoint\n\n- Define grid attributes on children themselves (&#96;data-grid&#96; key)\n\n- Static elements\n\n- Persistent id per item for predictable localstorage restores, even when # items changes\n\n- Min/max w/h per item\n\n- Resizable handles on other corners\n\n- Configurable w/h per breakpoint",

Here are the main differences between **react-grid-layout** (original) and **react-grid-layout-next** (fork):

---

## Differences

| Aspect | react-grid-layout (original) | react-grid-layout-next (fork) |
|--------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Language** | JavaScript + Flow | TypeScript |
| **Component style** | Class components | Functional components |
| **React 18** | v1 had issues; v2 fixed them | Explicit support |
| **Z-index** | Basic / implicit | Explicit handling for overlapping items |
| **API** | v1 flat props; v2 hooks + composable config | Same v1-style API as original |
| **Maintenance** | Active (v2.2.2, Dec 2025) | Stale (last update ~June 2023) |

---

## What the fork changed

From the [react-grid-layout-next README](https://github.com/dao-xyz/react-grid-layout-next):

1. **Functional React in TypeScript** – Replaced JavaScript + Flow with TypeScript and functional components.
2. **React 18 support** – Added compatibility when the original had React 18 issues.
3. **Z-index for overlapping items** – Better control when items overlap (e.g. during drag).
4. **Faster iteration** – Monorepo (Lerna) and structure aimed at easier development.

---

## Timeline

- **react-grid-layout-next** (2023): Fork created to address React 18 and TypeScript needs before the original v2.
- **react-grid-layout v2** (2024–2025): Official v2 added TypeScript, hooks, React 18 support, and a new API.

---

## Summary

The fork was a temporary solution for React 18 and TypeScript. The original library’s v2 now covers those needs and more (hooks, composable config, tree-shaking). The fork is no longer maintained and has no clear advantage over the official v2.

Rendering Modes\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Mode                  | Where        | When to Use                               |\\\\\\\\n| --------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\n| **Server Components** | Server only  | Data fetching, heavy computation, secrets |\\\\\\\\n| **Client Components** | Browser      | Interactivity, hooks, browser APIs        |\\\\\\\\n| **Static**            | Build time   | Content that rarely changes               |\\\\\\\\n| **Dynamic**           | Request time | Personalized or real-time data            |\\\\\\\\n| **Streaming**         | Progressive  | Large pages, slow data sources            |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. Hero (Above the Fold)\\\\\\\\n- Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).\\\\\\\\n- Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.\\\\\\\\n- Primary CTAs: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"View projects\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" (scroll to Projects) and \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Download resume\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" (link to static PDF in /public).\\\\\\\\n- A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 3. On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 5. Experience (Static)\\\\\\\\nChronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 8. Group related routes together without affecting the URL structure (e.g., marketing pages vs admin pages)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Multiple layouts for different sections** - You can have different &#96;layout.tsx&#96; files in each route group:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── (marketing)/\\\\\\\\n│   ├── layout.tsx    ← Marketing layout (maybe full-width, colorful)\\\\\\\\n│   └── about/page.tsx\\\\\\\\n├── (admin)/\\\\\\\\n│   ├── layout.tsx    ← Admin layout (sidebar, dashboard style)\\\\\\\\n│   └── dashboard/page.tsx\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Multiple root layouts** - You can even have multiple root layouts by placing different &#96;layout.tsx&#96; files in different route groups at the top level\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n4. **Better code organization** - Keep related files together without polluting your URL structure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Example Use Case\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf you want your marketing pages to have a public header/footer and your admin pages to have a dashboard sidebar, route groups let you apply different layouts without changing URLs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"│   └── settings/\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":52},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"│       └── page.tsx      → /settings\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":53},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"└── page.tsx              → /\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":54},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":55},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":56},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Notice how &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(admin)&#96; don't appear in the URLs at all.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":57},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":58},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"### What Are They Used For?\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":59},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":60},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"1. **Organizing routes by section/intent/team** - Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9.
