Project structure and organization\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis page provides an overview of **all** the folder and file conventions in Next.js, and recommendations for organizing your project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Folder and file conventions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Top-level folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTop-level folders are used to organize your application's code and static assets.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route segments to path segments](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/top-level-folders.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                    |                                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;app&#96;](/docs/app.md)                                                 | App Router                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;pages&#96;](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing.md)           | Pages Router                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;public&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/public-folder.md) | Static assets to be served         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;src&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder.md)       | Optional application source folder |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Top-level files\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTop-level files are used to configure your application, manage dependencies, run proxy, integrate monitoring tools, and define environment variables.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                              |                                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| **Next.js**                                                                  |                                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;next.config.js&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js.md)            | Configuration file for Next.js          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;package.json&#96;](/docs/app/getting-started/installation.md#manual-installation) | Project dependencies and scripts        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;instrumentation.ts&#96;](/docs/app/guides/instrumentation.md)                     | OpenTelemetry and Instrumentation file  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;proxy.ts&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy.md)                 | Next.js request proxy                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                             | Environment variables                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.local&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                       | Local environment variables             |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.production&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                  | Production environment variables        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.development&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                 | Development environment variables       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;eslint.config.mjs&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint.md)                 | Configuration file for ESLint           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;.gitignore&#96;                                                                 | Git files and folders to ignore         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;next-env.d.ts&#96;                                                              | TypeScript declaration file for Next.js |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;tsconfig.json&#96;                                                              | Configuration file for TypeScript       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;jsconfig.json&#96;                                                              | Configuration file for JavaScript       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Routing Files\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAdd &#96;page&#96; to expose a route, &#96;layout&#96; for shared UI such as header, nav, or footer, &#96;loading&#96; for skeletons, &#96;error&#96; for error boundaries, and &#96;route&#96; for APIs.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                               |                     |                              |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;layout&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout.md)                   | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Layout                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;page&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page.md)                       | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Page                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;loading&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading.md)                 | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Loading UI                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;not-found&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found.md)             | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Not found UI                 |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;error&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error.md)                     | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Error UI                     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;global-error&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error.md#global-error) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Global error UI              |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;route&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route.md)                     | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96;         | API endpoint                 |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;template&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/template.md)               | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Re-rendered layout           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;default&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default.md)                 | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Parallel route fallback page |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Nested routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFolders define URL segments. Nesting folders nests segments. Layouts at any level wrap their child segments. A route becomes public when a &#96;page&#96; or &#96;route&#96; file exists.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                        | URL pattern     | Notes                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96;            | —               | Root layout wraps all routes  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/layout.tsx&#96;       | —               | Wraps &#96;/blog&#96; and descendants |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/page.tsx&#96;              | &#96;/&#96;             | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/page.tsx&#96;         | &#96;/blog&#96;         | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/authors/page.tsx&#96; | &#96;/blog/authors&#96; | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Dynamic routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nParameterize segments with square brackets. Use &#96;[segment]&#96; for a single param, &#96;[...segment]&#96; for catch‑all, and &#96;[[...segment]]&#96; for optional catch‑all. Access values via the [&#96;params&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page.md#params-optional) prop.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                            | URL pattern                                                          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/blog/my-first-post&#96;                                                |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx&#96;   | &#96;/shop/clothing&#96;, &#96;/shop/clothing/shirts&#96;                            |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx&#96; | &#96;/docs&#96;, &#96;/docs/layouts-and-pages&#96;, &#96;/docs/api-reference/use-router&#96; |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Route groups and private folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOrganize code without changing URLs with route groups [&#96;(group)&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups.md#convention), and colocate non-routable files with private folders [&#96;_folder&#96;](#private-folders).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                            | URL pattern | Notes                                     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/(marketing)/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/&#96;         | Group omitted from URL                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/(shop)/cart/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/cart&#96;     | Share layouts within &#96;(shop)&#96;             |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/_components/Post.tsx&#96; | —           | Not routable; safe place for UI utilities |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/_lib/data.ts&#96;         | —           | Not routable; safe place for utils        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Parallel and Intercepted Routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese features fit specific UI patterns, such as slot-based layouts or modal routing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nUse &#96;@slot&#96; for named slots rendered by a parent layout. Use intercept patterns to render another route inside the current layout without changing the URL, for example, to show a details view as a modal over a list.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Pattern (docs)                                                                              | Meaning              | Typical use case                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;@folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes.md#slots)                 | Named slot           | Sidebar + main content                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(.)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)      | Intercept same level | Preview sibling route in a modal         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(..)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)     | Intercept parent     | Open a child of the parent as an overlay |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(..)(..)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention) | Intercept two levels | Deeply nested overlay                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(...)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)    | Intercept from root  | Show arbitrary route in current view     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Metadata file conventions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### App icons\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Icon file      |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;apple-icon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#generate-icons-using-code-js-ts-tsx) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96;                  | Generated Apple App Icon |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### Open Graph and Twitter images\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Generated Open Graph image |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;twitter-image&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image.md#twitter-image)                          | &#96;.jpg&#96; Generated Twitter image    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### SEO\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                                                              |             |                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;sitemap&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap.md#sitemap-files-xml)                     | &#96;.xml&#96;      | Sitemap file |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;robots&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots.md#static-robotstxt)                        | &#96;.txt&#96;      | Robots file           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;robots&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots.md#generate-a-robots-file)                  | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; | Generated Robots file |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Organizing your project\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext.js is **unopinionated** about how you organize and colocate your project files. But it does provide several features to help you organize your project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Component hierarchy\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe components defined in special files are rendered in a specific hierarchy:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;layout.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;template.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;error.js&#96; (React error boundary)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;loading.js&#96; (React suspense boundary)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;not-found.js&#96; (React error boundary for \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"not found\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" UI)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;page.js&#96; or nested &#96;layout.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Component Hierarchy for File Conventions](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe components are rendered recursively in nested routes, meaning the components of a route segment will be nested **inside** the components of its parent segment.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Nested File Conventions Component Hierarchy](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Colocation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIn the &#96;app&#96; directory, nested folders define route structure. Each folder represents a route segment that is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nHowever, even though route structure is defined through folders, a route is **not publicly accessible** until a &#96;page.js&#96; or &#96;route.js&#96; file is added to a route segment.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing how a route is not publicly accessible until a page.js or route.js file is added to a route segment.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-not-routable.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAnd, even when a route is made publicly accessible, only the **content returned** by &#96;page.js&#96; or &#96;route.js&#96; is sent to the client.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing how page.js and route.js files make routes publicly accessible.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-routable.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis means that **project files** can be **safely colocated** inside route segments in the &#96;app&#96; directory without accidentally being routable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing colocated project files are not routable even when a segment contains a page.js or route.js file.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-colocation.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**: While you **can** colocate your project files in &#96;app&#96; you don't **have** to. If you prefer, you can [keep them outside the &#96;app&#96; directory](#store-project-files-outside-of-app).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Private folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPrivate folders can be created by prefixing a folder with an underscore: &#96;_folderName&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis indicates the folder is a private implementation detail and should not be considered by the routing system, thereby **opting the folder and all its subfolders** out of routing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure using private folders](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-private-folders.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSince files in the &#96;app&#96; directory can be [safely colocated by default](#colocation), private folders are not required for colocation. However, they can be useful for:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Separating UI logic from routing logic.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Consistently organizing internal files across a project and the Next.js ecosystem.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Sorting and grouping files in code editors.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Avoiding potential naming conflicts with future Next.js file conventions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * While not a framework convention, you might also consider marking files outside private folders as \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"private\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" using the same underscore pattern.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * You can create URL segments that start with an underscore by prefixing the folder name with &#96;%5F&#96; (the URL-encoded form of an underscore): &#96;%5FfolderName&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * If you don't use private folders, it would be helpful to know Next.js [special file conventions](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure.md#routing-files) to prevent unexpected naming conflicts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Route groups\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRoute groups can be created by wrapping a folder in parenthesis: &#96;(folderName)&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure using route groups](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRoute groups are useful for:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Organizing routes by site section, intent, or team. e.g. marketing pages, admin pages, etc.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Enabling nested layouts in the same route segment level:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  * [Creating multiple nested layouts in the same segment, including multiple root layouts](#creating-multiple-root-layouts)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  * [Adding a layout to a subset of routes in a common segment](#opting-specific-segments-into-a-layout)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### &#96;src&#96; folder\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext.js supports storing application code (including &#96;app&#96;) inside an optional [&#96;src&#96; folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder.md). This separates application code from project configuration files which mostly live in the root of a project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with the src folder](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-src-directory.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Examples\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe following section lists a very high-level overview of common strategies. The simplest takeaway is to choose a strategy that works for you and your team and be consistent across the project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**: In our examples below, we're using &#96;components&#96; and &#96;lib&#96; folders as generalized placeholders, their naming has no special framework significance and your projects might use other folders like &#96;ui&#96;, &#96;utils&#96;, &#96;hooks&#96;, &#96;styles&#96;, etc.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Store project files outside of &#96;app&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of your project** and keeps the &#96;app&#96; directory purely for routing purposes.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files outside of app](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-project-root.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Store project files in top-level folders inside of &#96;app&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of the &#96;app&#96; directory**.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files inside app](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-app-root.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Split project files by feature or route\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores globally shared application code in the root &#96;app&#96; directory and **splits** more specific application code into the route segments that use them.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files split by feature or route](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-app-root-split.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Organize routes without affecting the URL path\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. &#96;(marketing)&#96; or &#96;(shop)&#96;).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Organizing Routes with Route Groups](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-organisation.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEven though routes inside &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(shop)&#96; share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a &#96;layout.js&#96; file inside their folders.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Multiple Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-multiple-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Opting specific segments into a layout\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. &#96;(shop)&#96;) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. &#96;account&#96; and &#96;cart&#96;). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. &#96;checkout&#96;).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Opt-in Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Opting for loading skeletons on a specific route\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo apply a [loading skeleton](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading.md) via a &#96;loading.js&#96; file to a specific route, create a new route group (e.g., &#96;/(overview)&#96;) and then move your &#96;loading.tsx&#96; inside that route group.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Folder structure showing a loading.tsx and a page.tsx inside the route group](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-loading.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNow, the &#96;loading.tsx&#96; file will only apply to your dashboard → overview page instead of all your dashboard pages without affecting the URL path structure.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Creating multiple root layouts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo create multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout.md#root-layout), remove the top-level &#96;layout.js&#96; file, and add a &#96;layout.js&#96; file inside each route group. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The &#96;\u003chtml\u003e&#96; and &#96;\u003cbody\u003e&#96; tags need to be added to each root layout.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Multiple Root Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIn the example above, both &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(shop)&#96; have their own root layout.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"}\\\\\\\\n\u003c/details\u003e\\\\\\\\n\u003c/tool-use\u003e\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003cthink\u003e\u003cdetails\u003e\u003csummary\u003eThought Process\u003c/summary\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\" documentation.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":530},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Three actions: 1) 'get' - Fetch full docs with a path (preferred after init). 2) 'search' - Find docs by keyword (redirects to use llms.txt index if init was called). 3) 'force-search' - Bypass init check and force API search (escape hatch only).\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":531},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"After calling init, prefer using 'get' directly with paths from the llms.txt index.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":532},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":533},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"*Parameters*:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":534},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  * action: get\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":535},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  * path: /docs/app/getting-started/project-structure\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":536},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":537},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"*Result*:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":538},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"{\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"path\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"anchor\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":null,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"url\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"# Project structure and organization\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis page provides an overview of **all** the folder and file conventions in Next.js, and recommendations for organizing your project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Folder and file conventions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Top-level folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTop-level folders are used to organize your application's code and static assets.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route segments to path segments](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/top-level-folders.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                    |                                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;app&#96;](/docs/app.md)                                                 | App Router                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;pages&#96;](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing.md)           | Pages Router                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;public&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/public-folder.md) | Static assets to be served         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;src&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder.md)       | Optional application source folder |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Top-level files\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTop-level files are used to configure your application, manage dependencies, run proxy, integrate monitoring tools, and define environment variables.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                              |                                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| **Next.js**                                                                  |                                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;next.config.js&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js.md)            | Configuration file for Next.js          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;package.json&#96;](/docs/app/getting-started/installation.md#manual-installation) | Project dependencies and scripts        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;instrumentation.ts&#96;](/docs/app/guides/instrumentation.md)                     | OpenTelemetry and Instrumentation file  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;proxy.ts&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy.md)                 | Next.js request proxy                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                             | Environment variables                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.local&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                       | Local environment variables             |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.production&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                  | Production environment variables        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;.env.development&#96;](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables.md)                 | Development environment variables       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;eslint.config.mjs&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint.md)                 | Configuration file for ESLint           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;.gitignore&#96;                                                                 | Git files and folders to ignore         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;next-env.d.ts&#96;                                                              | TypeScript declaration file for Next.js |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;tsconfig.json&#96;                                                              | Configuration file for TypeScript       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;jsconfig.json&#96;                                                              | Configuration file for JavaScript       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Routing Files\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAdd &#96;page&#96; to expose a route, &#96;layout&#96; for shared UI such as header, nav, or footer, &#96;loading&#96; for skeletons, &#96;error&#96; for error boundaries, and &#96;route&#96; for APIs.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                               |                     |                              |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;layout&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout.md)                   | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Layout                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;page&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page.md)                       | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Page                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;loading&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading.md)                 | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Loading UI                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;not-found&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found.md)             | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Not found UI                 |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;error&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error.md)                     | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Error UI                     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;global-error&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error.md#global-error) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Global error UI              |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;route&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route.md)                     | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96;         | API endpoint                 |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;template&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/template.md)               | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Re-rendered layout           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;default&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default.md)                 | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.jsx&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96; | Parallel route fallback page |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Nested routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nFolders define URL segments. Nesting folders nests segments. Layouts at any level wrap their child segments. A route becomes public when a &#96;page&#96; or &#96;route&#96; file exists.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                        | URL pattern     | Notes                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96;            | —               | Root layout wraps all routes  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/layout.tsx&#96;       | —               | Wraps &#96;/blog&#96; and descendants |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/page.tsx&#96;              | &#96;/&#96;             | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/page.tsx&#96;         | &#96;/blog&#96;         | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/authors/page.tsx&#96; | &#96;/blog/authors&#96; | Public route                  |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Dynamic routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nParameterize segments with square brackets. Use &#96;[segment]&#96; for a single param, &#96;[...segment]&#96; for catch‑all, and &#96;[[...segment]]&#96; for optional catch‑all. Access values via the [&#96;params&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page.md#params-optional) prop.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                            | URL pattern                                                          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/blog/my-first-post&#96;                                                |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx&#96;   | &#96;/shop/clothing&#96;, &#96;/shop/clothing/shirts&#96;                            |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx&#96; | &#96;/docs&#96;, &#96;/docs/layouts-and-pages&#96;, &#96;/docs/api-reference/use-router&#96; |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Route groups and private folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOrganize code without changing URLs with route groups [&#96;(group)&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups.md#convention), and colocate non-routable files with private folders [&#96;_folder&#96;](#private-folders).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Path                            | URL pattern | Notes                                     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/(marketing)/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/&#96;         | Group omitted from URL                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/(shop)/cart/page.tsx&#96;      | &#96;/cart&#96;     | Share layouts within &#96;(shop)&#96;             |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/_components/Post.tsx&#96; | —           | Not routable; safe place for UI utilities |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| &#96;app/blog/_lib/data.ts&#96;         | —           | Not routable; safe place for utils        |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Parallel and Intercepted Routes\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThese features fit specific UI patterns, such as slot-based layouts or modal routing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nUse &#96;@slot&#96; for named slots rendered by a parent layout. Use intercept patterns to render another route inside the current layout without changing the URL, for example, to show a details view as a modal over a list.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| Pattern (docs)                                                                              | Meaning              | Typical use case                         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;@folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes.md#slots)                 | Named slot           | Sidebar + main content                   |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(.)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)      | Intercept same level | Preview sibling route in a modal         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(..)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)     | Intercept parent     | Open a child of the parent as an overlay |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(..)(..)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention) | Intercept two levels | Deeply nested overlay                    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;(...)folder&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes.md#convention)    | Intercept from root  | Show arbitrary route in current view     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Metadata file conventions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### App icons\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                                                                 |                                     |                          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;favicon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#favicon)                                | &#96;.ico&#96;                              | Favicon file             |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;icon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#icon)                                      | &#96;.ico&#96; &#96;.jpg&#96; &#96;.jpeg&#96; &#96;.png&#96; &#96;.svg&#96; | App Icon file            |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;icon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#generate-icons-using-code-js-ts-tsx)       | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96;                  | Generated App Icon       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;apple-icon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#apple-icon)                          | &#96;.jpg&#96; &#96;.jpeg&#96;, &#96;.png&#96;              | Apple App Icon file      |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;apple-icon&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons.md#generate-icons-using-code-js-ts-tsx) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96;                  | Generated Apple App Icon |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### Open Graph and Twitter images\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                                                                             |                              |                            |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;opengraph-image&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image.md#opengraph-image)                      | &#96;.jpg&#96; &#96;.jpeg&#96; &#96;.png&#96; &#96;.gif&#96; | Open Graph image file      |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;opengraph-image&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image.md#generate-images-using-code-js-ts-tsx) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96;           | Generated Open Graph image |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;twitter-image&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image.md#twitter-image)                          | &#96;.jpg&#96; &#96;.jpeg&#96; &#96;.png&#96; &#96;.gif&#96; | Twitter image file         |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;twitter-image&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image.md#generate-images-using-code-js-ts-tsx)   | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; &#96;.tsx&#96;           | Generated Twitter image    |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n#### SEO\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n|                                                                                                              |             |                       |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------- |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;sitemap&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap.md#sitemap-files-xml)                     | &#96;.xml&#96;      | Sitemap file          |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;sitemap&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap.md#generating-a-sitemap-using-code-js-ts) | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; | Generated Sitemap     |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;robots&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots.md#static-robotstxt)                        | &#96;.txt&#96;      | Robots file           |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n| [&#96;robots&#96;](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots.md#generate-a-robots-file)                  | &#96;.js&#96; &#96;.ts&#96; | Generated Robots file |\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Organizing your project\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext.js is **unopinionated** about how you organize and colocate your project files. But it does provide several features to help you organize your project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Component hierarchy\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe components defined in special files are rendered in a specific hierarchy:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;layout.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;template.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;error.js&#96; (React error boundary)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;loading.js&#96; (React suspense boundary)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;not-found.js&#96; (React error boundary for \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"not found\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" UI)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* &#96;page.js&#96; or nested &#96;layout.js&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Component Hierarchy for File Conventions](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe components are rendered recursively in nested routes, meaning the components of a route segment will be nested **inside** the components of its parent segment.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Nested File Conventions Component Hierarchy](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/nested-file-conventions-component-hierarchy.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Colocation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIn the &#96;app&#96; directory, nested folders define route structure. Each folder represents a route segment that is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nHowever, even though route structure is defined through folders, a route is **not publicly accessible** until a &#96;page.js&#96; or &#96;route.js&#96; file is added to a route segment.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing how a route is not publicly accessible until a page.js or route.js file is added to a route segment.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-not-routable.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAnd, even when a route is made publicly accessible, only the **content returned** by &#96;page.js&#96; or &#96;route.js&#96; is sent to the client.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing how page.js and route.js files make routes publicly accessible.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-routable.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis means that **project files** can be **safely colocated** inside route segments in the &#96;app&#96; directory without accidentally being routable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![A diagram showing colocated project files are not routable even when a segment contains a page.js or route.js file.](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-colocation.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**: While you **can** colocate your project files in &#96;app&#96; you don't **have** to. If you prefer, you can [keep them outside the &#96;app&#96; directory](#store-project-files-outside-of-app).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Private folders\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPrivate folders can be created by prefixing a folder with an underscore: &#96;_folderName&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis indicates the folder is a private implementation detail and should not be considered by the routing system, thereby **opting the folder and all its subfolders** out of routing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure using private folders](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-private-folders.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nSince files in the &#96;app&#96; directory can be [safely colocated by default](#colocation), private folders are not required for colocation. However, they can be useful for:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Separating UI logic from routing logic.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Consistently organizing internal files across a project and the Next.js ecosystem.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Sorting and grouping files in code editors.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Avoiding potential naming conflicts with future Next.js file conventions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * While not a framework convention, you might also consider marking files outside private folders as \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"private\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" using the same underscore pattern.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * You can create URL segments that start with an underscore by prefixing the folder name with &#96;%5F&#96; (the URL-encoded form of an underscore): &#96;%5FfolderName&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * If you don't use private folders, it would be helpful to know Next.js [special file conventions](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure.md#routing-files) to prevent unexpected naming conflicts.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Route groups\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRoute groups can be created by wrapping a folder in parenthesis: &#96;(folderName)&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure using route groups](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRoute groups are useful for:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Organizing routes by site section, intent, or team. e.g. marketing pages, admin pages, etc.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* Enabling nested layouts in the same route segment level:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  * [Creating multiple nested layouts in the same segment, including multiple root layouts](#creating-multiple-root-layouts)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  * [Adding a layout to a subset of routes in a common segment](#opting-specific-segments-into-a-layout)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### &#96;src&#96; folder\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNext.js supports storing application code (including &#96;app&#96;) inside an optional [&#96;src&#96; folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder.md). This separates application code from project configuration files which mostly live in the root of a project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with the src folder](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-src-directory.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Examples\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThe following section lists a very high-level overview of common strategies. The simplest takeaway is to choose a strategy that works for you and your team and be consistent across the project.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**: In our examples below, we're using &#96;components&#96; and &#96;lib&#96; folders as generalized placeholders, their naming has no special framework significance and your projects might use other folders like &#96;ui&#96;, &#96;utils&#96;, &#96;hooks&#96;, &#96;styles&#96;, etc.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Store project files outside of &#96;app&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of your project** and keeps the &#96;app&#96; directory purely for routing purposes.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files outside of app](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-project-root.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Store project files in top-level folders inside of &#96;app&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores all application code in shared folders in the **root of the &#96;app&#96; directory**.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files inside app](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-app-root.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Split project files by feature or route\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis strategy stores globally shared application code in the root &#96;app&#96; directory and **splits** more specific application code into the route segments that use them.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![An example folder structure with project files split by feature or route](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/project-organization-app-root-split.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Organize routes without affecting the URL path\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. &#96;(marketing)&#96; or &#96;(shop)&#96;).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Organizing Routes with Route Groups](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-organisation.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nEven though routes inside &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(shop)&#96; share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a &#96;layout.js&#96; file inside their folders.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Multiple Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-multiple-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Opting specific segments into a layout\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. &#96;(shop)&#96;) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. &#96;account&#96; and &#96;cart&#96;). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. &#96;checkout&#96;).\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Opt-in Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-opt-in-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Opting for loading skeletons on a specific route\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo apply a [loading skeleton](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading.md) via a &#96;loading.js&#96; file to a specific route, create a new route group (e.g., &#96;/(overview)&#96;) and then move your &#96;loading.tsx&#96; inside that route group.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Folder structure showing a loading.tsx and a page.tsx inside the route group](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-loading.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nNow, the &#96;loading.tsx&#96; file will only apply to your dashboard → overview page instead of all your dashboard pages without affecting the URL path structure.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n### Creating multiple root layouts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nTo create multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout.md#root-layout), remove the top-level &#96;layout.js&#96; file, and add a &#96;layout.js&#96; file inside each route group. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The &#96;\u003chtml\u003e&#96; and &#96;\u003cbody\u003e&#96; tags need to be added to each root layout.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n![Route Groups with Multiple Root Layouts](https://h8DxKfmAPhn8O0p3.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/docs/light/route-group-multiple-root-layouts.png)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nIn the example above, both &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(shop)&#96; have their own root layout.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"}\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":539},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c/details\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":540},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c/tool-use\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":541},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":542},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":543},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":544},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003cthink\u003e\u003cdetails\u003e\u003csummary\u003eThought Process\u003c/summary\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":545}]},\\\\\\\"score\\\\\\\":0.27517589926719666},{\\\\\\\"codeBlock\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"relativeWorkspacePath\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"range\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"startPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":477,\\\\\\\"column\\\\\\\":1},\\\\\\\"endPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":520,\\\\\\\"column\\\\\\\":1}},\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{}},\\\\\\\"score\\\\\\\":0.27353379130363464},{\\\\\\\"codeBlock\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"relativeWorkspacePath\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-12-01_12-07Z-understanding-folder-structure-in-next-js.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"range\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"startPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":51},\\\\\\\"endPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":84}},\\\\\\\"contents\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"│   └── settings/\\\\\\\\n│       └── page.tsx      → /settings\\\\\\\\n└── page.tsx              → /\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNotice how &#96;(marketing)&#96; and &#96;(admin)&#96; don't appear in the URLs at all.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### What Are They Used For?\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. **Organizing routes by section/intent/team** - Group related routes together without affecting the URL structure (e.g., marketing pages vs admin pages)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n2. **Multiple layouts for different sections** - You can have different &#96;layout.tsx&#96; files in each route group:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── (marketing)/\\\\\\\\n│   ├── layout.tsx    ← Marketing layout (maybe full-width, colorful)\\\\\\\\n│   └── about/page.tsx\\\\\\\\n├── (admin)/\\\\\\\\n│   ├── layout.tsx    ← Admin layout (sidebar, dashboard style)\\\\\\\\n│   └── dashboard/page.tsx\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n3. **Multiple root layouts** - You can even have multiple root layouts by placing different &#96;layout.tsx&#96; files in different route groups at the top level\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n4. **Better code organization** - Keep related files together without polluting your URL structure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Example Use Case\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf you want your marketing pages to have a public header/footer and your admin pages to have a dashboard sidebar, route groups let you apply different layouts without changing URLs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"│   └── settings/\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":52},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"│       └── page.tsx      → /settings\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":53},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"└── page.tsx              → /\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":54},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":55},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":56},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Notice how &#96;(marketing)&#96; files in different route groups at the top level\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":75},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":76},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"4. **Better code organization** - Keep related files together without polluting your URL structure\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":77},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":78},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"### Example Use Case\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":79},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":80},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"If you want your marketing pages to have a public header/footer and your admin pages to have a dashboard sidebar, route groups let you apply different layouts without changing URLs.\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":81},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":82},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":83}]},\\\\\\\"score\\\\\\\":0.2673148512840271},{\\\\\\\"codeBlock\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"relativeWorkspacePath\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"./.specstory/history/2025-12-01_10-48Z-static-portfolio-website-design-specifications.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"range\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"startPosition\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"endPosition\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"line\\\\\\\":18}},\\\\\\\"contents\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --\u003e\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003c!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --\u003e\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nInterprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCreate a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system \u0026 visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing \u0026 grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance \u0026 best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Import Tailwind in your CSS with &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;, not &#96;@tailwind&#96; directives.- Define design tokens, custom utilities, and settings in CSS using the new &#96;@theme&#96; at-rule and related directives (so there is no default &#96;tailwind.config.ts&#96;). If you intentionally want to keep a legacy JS/TS configuration, load it explicitly from CSS using &#96;@config \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"./tailwind.config.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (this is allowed for backward compatibility), but prefer CSS-first. - Use &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; for PostCSS setups or &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; when using Vite/Next dev tooling. Use &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; for CLI commands. - Keep compatibility with Tailwind v4 features: automatic content detection, CSS theme variables, container queries, and prefers-reduced-motion handling.Deliverables (explicit)- Output a complete project scaffold (files and code) ready to run with &#96;pnpm&#96;/&#96;npm&#96;:  - &#96;app/page.tsx&#96; (home)  - &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96; (meta, fonts, theme provider)  - &#96;components/*&#96; for each UI piece  - &#96;lib/data.ts&#96; or &#96;data/seed.ts&#96; with typed placeholder data  - &#96;public/&#96; with placeholder images (profile SVG) and &#96;resume.pdf&#96;  - &#96;styles/globals.css&#96; containing &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\";&#96; and your &#96;@theme&#96; declarations  - &#96;postcss.config.mjs&#96; referencing &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; if using PostCSS, or instructions to use &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; for Vite users  - &#96;package.json&#96; with &#96;tailwindcss&#96; v4 and &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; as appropriate- Include a small README with run instructions and notes about where to plug the CMS later (which files to replace).- Keep code neat, well-commented, and idiomatic TypeScript/React.Important constraints (do not implement)- Do not build the CMS, user authentication, or live edit features now. Only create the static visuals and seed data.- Do not include external analytics or tracking scripts.- Do not use non-free or proprietary fonts; prefer Google Fonts or system fallbacks.Tone for copywriting- Confident, concise, and human. Provide short placeholder copy for name, tagline, project descriptions, and experience bullets that reads like a senior engineer (you can use realistic but fictional content).Final note- Make the bento grids a signature element — they should be visually distinct, memorable, and adaptable so the future CMS can change tile sizes/content. Prioritize a pristine mobile experience, while delivering an elegant and airy desktop layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**Agent (model claude-4.5-opus-high-thinking, mode Agent)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"\u003c!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --\u003e\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Interprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":10},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":12},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Create a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. Rate Limiting\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Use Vercel WAF as the primary rate limiting layer** — operates at the edge with global state, before your code runs. In-memory counters (LRU, Map, better-auth &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"memory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; storage) are unreliable on serverless — instances don't share memory, cold starts reset counters.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Recommended WAF Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rule | Path | Limit | Window | Action |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Auth protection | &#96;/api/auth/*&#96; | 20 req | 60s | Deny (429) |\\\\\\\\n| General API | &#96;/api/*&#96; | 100 req | 60s | Deny (429) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Rules\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Enable better-auth rate limiting** as defense in depth — use &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"database\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; storage for production, &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"memory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; acceptable as basic deterrent for low-traffic single-admin\\\\\\\\n- **Stricter limits on auth endpoints** (10-20 req/min) — most targeted\\\\\\\\n- **Return &#96;429 Too Many Requests&#96;** with &#96;Retry-After&#96; header when possible\\\\\\\\n- **Use &#96;@vercel/firewall&#96; SDK** for application-level context (user ID, etc.) — requires matching dashboard rule\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n\u003e Full &#96;@vercel/firewall&#96; SDK examples and WAF plan limits: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#rate-limiting-details)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Source Maps \u0026 Production Hardening\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Never enable &#96;productionBrowserSourceMaps: true&#96;** — exposes source code\\\\\\\\n- **Add &#96;removeConsole&#96; to &#96;next.config.ts&#96;** — strips &#96;console.log&#96;/&#96;debug&#96;/&#96;info&#96;/&#96;trace&#96;, keeps &#96;error&#96;/&#96;warn&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Never log sensitive data** — tokens, passwords, DB URLs must never appear in logs\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Dependency Security\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Run &#96;pnpm audit&#96; before every deployment** — no high/critical vulnerabilities\\\\\\\\n- **&#96;pnpm up&#96; weekly** (within semver ranges), &#96;pnpm dlx npm-check-updates&#96; monthly (check majors)\\\\\\\\n- **Lock file is your friend** — always commit &#96;pnpm-lock.yaml&#96;\\\\\\\\n- **Ignore unfixable CVEs explicitly** in &#96;auditConfig.ignoreCves&#96; _**Agent (claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking)**_

This is an important architectural decision. Let me break down both approaches for your specific use case.

---

## Option A: Single page + nuqs filter (recommended)

One page, one grid. The navbar updates a `?section=projects` query param via [nuqs](https://nuqs.dev/). The grid reacts by:

1. **Reorganizing** items (filtered section items move to the top)
2. **Expanding** to show all items of that section (not just the 3 from the overview)
3. **Fading** unrelated items out or hiding them entirely

```
URL: /                        → All sections, limited items each
URL: /?section=projects       → Projects first + all projects visible
URL: /?section=experience     → Experiences first + all visible
URL: /?section=contact        → Contact cards highlighted
```

### How it works

- `react-grid-layout` handles repositioning with built-in CSS transform animations
- nuqs syncs the filter state to the URL (shareable, back-button friendly)
- When `section` changes, you compute a new `layouts` object with different item positions and visibility
- Items entering/leaving animate via Motion (fade in/out, scale)

### Pros

- Fluid, animated experience (no page loads, no route transitions)
- URL is shareable (`gonzalopozo.dev/?section=projects`)
- Back button works naturally (nuqs handles history)
- Single data fetch — all entities loaded once via RSC, grid is a client component
- `react-grid-layout` animates repositioning for free (CSS transforms)
- Closest to the Nev Flynn feel

### Cons

- Initial page loads all data (mitigated: your dataset is small — a few projects, experiences, skills)
- Grid logic is more complex (computing layouts per filter state)

---

## Option B: Separate pages with View Transitions

Each section is a different route:

```
/                    → Overview grid (3 projects, 3 experiences, etc.)
/projects            → Full projects grid
/experience          → Full experience grid
```

### How it works

- Next.js App Router routes with shared layout
- View Transitions API (experimental) or Motion `AnimatePresence` for page transitions
- Each page fetches only its data

### Pros

- Simpler per-page logic
- Better code splitting (each page loads its own data)
- SEO-friendly separate URLs

### Cons

- Page transitions in Next.js are still rough — View Transitions API is experimental and not well supported in all browsers
- Harder to make it feel as fluid as a single-page grid
- You lose the "grid reorganization" animation (items can't smoothly move from one position to another across page navigations)
- Layout shift between pages

---

## Why Option A fits your case better

Your key requirement is this:

> "3 projects in the main grid, click Projects, they reorganize and more appear"

This is fundamentally a **layout transition within a single grid**, not a page navigation. `react-grid-layout` animates item repositioning natively — items slide from position A to position B when the layout changes. You can't get that effect across separate pages.

### The flow would be:

```
User lands on /
  → Grid shows: Bio, Status, 3 Projects, 3 Experiences, Skills, Contact
  → Navbar: [Todo] [Sobre mí] [Proyectos] [Experiencia] [Contacto]

User clicks "Proyectos"
  → URL becomes /?section=projects (via nuqs)
  → Grid animates:
    - Project cards slide to top positions
    - Hidden projects (4, 5, 6...) fade in
    - Non-project cards either fade out or move below
  → Navbar: [Todo] [Sobre mí] [*Proyectos*] [Experiencia] [Contacto]

User clicks "Todo"
  → URL becomes / (nuqs clears param)
  → Grid animates back to overview layout
  → Extra projects fade out, cards return to original positions
```

---

## Architecture sketch

```
app/(public)/page.tsx          ← RSC: fetches all data
  └─ <PortfolioGrid>          ← Client component ("use client")
       ├─ useQueryState("section")   ← nuqs
       ├─ computeLayout(section, data)  ← returns react-grid-layout layouts
       └─ <ResponsiveGridLayout>
            ├─ <BioCard />
            ├─ <ProjectCard /> × N
            ├─ <ExperienceCard /> × N
            ├─ <SkillsCard />
            └─ <ContactCard />
```

The server component fetches everything once. The client component handles filtering, layout computation, and animation — all driven by the URL via nuqs.

---

## Summary

| Criteria | Option A (nuqs + single grid) | Option B (separate pages) |
|----------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Grid reorganization animation | Smooth (native) | Not possible |
| URL state | `/?section=projects` | `/projects` |
| Back button | Works (nuqs) | Works (router) |
| Fluid feel | Like Nev Flynn | Page-transition dependent |
| Complexity | Grid layout logic | Route + transition setup |
| Data loading | All at once (small dataset) | Per page |
| **Recommendation** | **This one** | |

Go with **Option A**: single page, nuqs for URL state, `react-grid-layout` for animated repositioning. It's the only way to get that smooth "cards reorganize and new ones appear" effect you described.
